summary: Independently reviewed all five candidates at commit 08124e6286ff09843500a35120a38a685806a646. Confirmed web-ui-001. The other four underlying defects reproduced, but their required attacker or authorization boundaries remain unverified. Both bounded isolated probes passed; no source fixes, live services, database writes, or exhaustion tests were performed.

verdicts.rationale: A contributor-controlled test title reaches an uncapped synchronous expansion during ordinary text surveying. A short, accepted range can demand impractical CPU and memory before focus output limits apply. The complete denial-of-service chain is established statically; the runtime probe verified only small-range behavior and rejection controls.

attacker_control.reason: A contributor can place a numbered title in a test file belonging to an existing surveyed package. Surveying parses its text without executing that file.

evidence.detail: Reads source files beneath the package selected by the story title.
calledTitles extracts call-argument strings from source text.
The title grammar accepts numeric ranges with attacker-selected endpoints.

reachability.reason: The registered focus tool surveys the current checkout. Desktop surveying reaches the same parser through main-process IPC.

evidence.detail: The focus handler invokes focusProject.
readMap invokes codeSurveyReader with checkout current before building the graph; focusProject awaits readMap.
The reader invokes surveyStory on loaded source text.
Surveyed test titles are passed to proofTitles.
The code-survey IPC handler invokes readCodeSurvey in the Electron main process.

trust_boundary.reason: Repository text, which need not be authorized for execution, controls synchronous work and allocation in the trusted survey process.

evidence.detail: Validation checks safe integers, equal capability numbers and ordering, but does not bound the span.
An uninterrupted loop inserts one string per integer through the supplied endpoint.

impact.reason: Static proof establishes resource consumption proportional to the numeric span, despite a short input. Map requests cannot complete during expansion; the desktop path can block its main event loop. Process termination and exhaustion thresholds were not tested.

evidence.detail: The expanded Set is additionally converted into an array of proof objects.
Focus runs only after the complete map read finishes.
The show ceiling is applied after surveying and graph construction.
The main-process handler directly awaits the shared survey reader.

counterevidence: Descending, cross-capability and unsafe-integer ranges are rejected.
Desktop main-mode surveying uses fetched origin/main when origin exists; unmerged checkout content reaches the current-checkout map path, not that normal desktop path.
Git deadlines and output limits bound subprocess work, not the subsequent JavaScript expansion.
The file must belong to a package selected by a project story.
test_evidence: Exit 0. Real surveyStory expanded 3.1–3.3 into exactly three identities and rejected descending, cross-capability and unsafe-endpoint controls.
Evidence: evidence/challenge-map-20261007T120906496922/stdout.txt:1. Preserved script, exact isolated command, source commit, exit status and stderr accompany it in the same directory.
test_limitations: No large accepted range, resource-exhaustion demonstration, Electron process or live map service was executed.
Large-span impact and desktop execution context are established statically.
verdicts.remediation: Apply a small expansion budget before entering the loop, including cumulative limits across a title or file, or represent ranges compactly. Skip oversized ranges without aborting unrelated surveys.
verdicts.regression_test_recommendation: Retain the small positive and rejection controls. After implementing a limit, verify that just-over-limit and very large safe-integer endpoints are rejected before enumeration, while unrelated files still survey.

verdicts.severity: medium if an untrusted recording supply path is established
verdicts.rationale: The real snapshot-to-render pipeline preserves malformed health strings and emits injected markup. However, the reviewed source establishes a local recording workflow, not an accepted external supplier route. Website script execution and deployed CSP are also unverified.

attacker_control.reason: Whoever supplies the selected record file controls its health strings, but an attacker’s ability to supply a recording accepted for publication was not established.

evidence.detail: A local command selects the record file and repository.
JSON is parsed and checked for project equality, without runtime health validation.
Ordinary health records require passing, failing or not-checked.

reachability.reason: Conditional on selecting and publishing the recording with its public reading, the source connects the imported tree to the website panel without health-state validation.

evidence.detail: The imported tree is forwarded to refreshGrowthSnapshot.
When arcs are supplied, the snapshot includes publicPlan(tree), then passes through scrub.
Contract health is retained wholesale.
growthReading exposes the saved public tree to website surfaces.
StoryDetails assigns renderStoryPanel output to innerHTML.

trust_boundary.reason: The data-to-HTML transition is proven, but the preceding transition from a less-trusted supplier into authorized publication remains unestablished.

evidence.detail: The contract’s reported state is copied directly into the rendering model.
badge interpolates state into a quoted class attribute without escaping.
Publication source selection restricts accepted runs to successful repository main/merged sources; this is not a public recording-upload interface.

impact.reason: Markup injection is established in the real pipeline, with a static innerHTML sink. Page-content injection follows if the malformed recording is published and the capability opened. Browser event-handler execution, credential access and account compromise were not demonstrated.

evidence.detail: Selected capability contracts render their reported state through badge.
An attribute-breaking state can terminate the span opening tag and introduce another element.
The generated string is consumed as HTML.

counterevidence: The real ordinary-health schema rejects the payload.
Free-text titles are escaped; that positive control passed.
The contract payload was absent when no capability was selected.
The snapshot has no public panel reading when arcs are omitted.
Desktop CSP at apps/desktop/src/renderer/index.html:5 excludes inline event handlers.
No external recording acceptance workflow was established.
test_evidence: Exit 0. Real refreshGrowthSnapshot, growthReading, drillDown and renderStoryPanel retained the malformed state and emitted an img element string carrying an onerror attribute.
All three valid states rendered normally. Escaped-title, unselected-capability, absent-public-reading and schema-rejection controls passed.
Evidence: evidence/challenge-publication-20261007T121006147313/stdout.txt:1 and :2. Script, exact isolated command, source commit, status and stderr are preserved alongside it.
test_limitations: The refresh CLI, build, publisher and browser were not executed.
The probe used synthetic JSON-derived data and a disposable snapshot file.
External supplier acceptance and deployed website CSP remain unknown.
verdicts.remediation: Validate imported recordings at runtime before publication. Convert health/status values through explicit allowed-value mappings and escape attribute interpolations defensively.
verdicts.regression_test_recommendation: Reject malformed imported states or render them inertly. Preserve all valid-state and free-text escaping controls. Add a bounded browser test under the actual website CSP once that deployment context is available.

verdicts.severity: low to medium if unauthorized disclosure is established
verdicts.rationale: The current-checkout reader follows a source-file symlink and returns external test-title metadata through real focusProject output. A recipient lacking access to that external data, or an automatic return channel to the contributor, was not established.

attacker_control.reason: A repository contributor can supply a matching source-file symlink. Its target must resolve and be readable on the surveying machine.

evidence.detail: filesUnder checks directory status and filename extension but does not require entry.file.
stat follows the symlink, and the resulting read uses the same path.

reachability.reason: Current-checkout focus reads use the vulnerable disk reader, retain parsed titles, and expose requested rows as structured tool data or CLI JSON.

evidence.detail: readMap explicitly selects checkout current.
fileAt reads the selected filesystem content.
Test graph nodes retain file.titles as testTitles.
The focus answer, including requested rows, is returned as response data.
Response data is included in structuredContent.

trust_boundary.reason: Filesystem containment is bypassed, but containment is not itself proof of unauthorized disclosure. The supplied front door is a local stdio tool; no lower-authority recipient or contributor-accessible result channel was established.

evidence.detail: The disk reader performs no resolved-path containment check.
The supplied MCP entry point serves the local caller through stdio.
The Git snapshot reader excludes symbolic-link modes.

impact.reason: External metadata extraction reproduced, but unauthorized confidentiality loss did not. The demonstrated result contains recognized numbered test titles, not arbitrary complete file contents.

evidence.detail: Only recognized proof titles enter this metadata path.
Those titles are retained in structured graph data.
The default textual formatter does not print testTitles.

counterevidence: Normal desktop origin/main surveying excludes symlink blobs.
An inaccessible origin with no fetched main fails instead of falling back to checkout content.
Only parseable survey metadata was recovered.
A caller already authorized to read the target gains no additional access.
No automatic network exfiltration or contributor-visible output channel was identified.
test_evidence: challenge-map.mts passed through the mandated submitter, exit 0.
A synthetic external file containing a numbered title appeared in real focusProject rows through a symlink. Removing the link made the selection absent; an ordinary-file control remained readable.
Evidence: evidence/challenge-map-20261007T120906496922/stdout.txt:2; exact command and preserved script are in the same directory.
test_limitations: Both files were synthetic and readable inside isolation; recipient authorization was not simulated.
Directory symlinks, Windows junctions and race conditions were not tested.
verdicts.remediation: Reject source symlinks and symlinked directory components, or enforce resolved-path containment within explicit allowed roots. Preserve the intentional app/desktop source seam.
verdicts.regression_test_recommendation: Require omission or refusal of the synthetic external-file symlink while ordinary source still surveys. Add bounded package-root symlink and platform-junction cases, and verify Git-mode exclusion.

verdicts.severity: low; security significance depends on writer authority
verdicts.rationale: Constructor is valid planning input and reproducibly causes the complete project survey to reject. The security claim remains unverified because no restricted project-writer role distinct from trusted project-management authority was established.

attacker_control.reason: A caller with ordinary planning write access controls the story title. Constructor passes both the tool’s stated validation and the real story schema.

evidence.detail: Titles require only a nonempty string.
plan_story forwards the supplied title to library.addStory.
The story schema accepts a nonempty title without reserving Constructor.

reachability.reason: The stored title is retained in projectTree and used by every project survey. Both current-checkout and local-fallback readers reproduced the rejection.

evidence.detail: nodeOf returns the stored title unchanged.
Health annotation preserves the story fields.
Every story title is passed to packageOf and its result to path.join.
Desktop code surveying uses the same reader.

trust_boundary.reason: The invalid data-to-lookup transition is established. A security boundary between the title writer and an independently protected reader remains unverified; the supplied local planning interface gives its caller broad project-editing powers.

evidence.detail: The package alias table is an ordinary object.
Normalized constructor resolves to the inherited Object constructor.
The same planning interface permits editing existing plan records.
The supplied tool server uses local stdio rather than establishing a separate restricted remote writer.

impact.reason: A single poisoned story makes the entire survey reject with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE, preventing fresh map/survey results for that tree. A whole-desktop crash is not established.

evidence.detail: All stories are aggregated with Promise.all, so one path.join rejection rejects the project survey.
Focus awaits the failed map read.
Survey failures are retried independently.
Tree rendering proceeds using the retained survey.

counterevidence: This is inherited-property lookup, not prototype mutation or code execution.
The writer requires existing planning authority; no unauthenticated entry was found.
Desktop tree rendering does not wait for a successful fresh survey.
The reader recovered when the poisoned title was removed from the synthetic tree.
test_evidence: challenge-map.mts passed, exit 0: packageOf returned a function for Constructor and The Constructor; a mixed project rejected with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE in current and local-fallback modes.
Normal-title, explicit-alias and subsequent recovery controls passed.
challenge-publication.mts confirmed the real story schema accepts Constructor.
test_limitations: No planning tool, database write or Electron application was executed.
Restricted-writer permissions and affected multi-user deployment context remain unknown.
verdicts.remediation: Use a Map or an own-property lookup for aliases and guarantee that packageOf returns a string. Consider containing individual story survey failures.
verdicts.regression_test_recommendation: Verify Constructor and The Constructor resolve to string slugs, explicit aliases remain correct, and a mixed project containing those titles surveys successfully.

verdicts.severity: low if an untrusted restoration path is established
verdicts.rationale: Inherited story IDs reproducibly break forestScene with an ordinary empty survey, and static restoration code preserves such IDs. No attacker-controlled snapshot acceptance workflow was established; restoration is an authorized backup operation and refuses nonempty projects.

attacker_control.reason: A supplied snapshot can contain arbitrary string record IDs, but attacker influence over a snapshot selected for restoration was not established. Ordinary planning fields reject an explicit ID.

evidence.detail: Restoration copies each supplied record.id directly into the insert payload.
The database record ID is a text primary key, without a reserved-name restriction.
Ordinary story fields do not accept an id field.
Ordinary generated IDs use a type prefix and random hexadecimal suffix.

reachability.reason: Conditional on authorized restoration of such a snapshot, static source connects preserved IDs through projectTree to desktop forestScene. The renderer failure itself was executed.

evidence.detail: The public restore implementation forwards the snapshot to writeSnapshot.
Record listing maps records through current.
current preserves the record ID.
The tree node receives record.id unchanged.
The desktop tree callback invokes forestScene with the current survey.

trust_boundary.reason: The imported-ID-to-inherited-property transition is established, but a less-trusted snapshot supplier crossing into an authorized restore workflow remains hypothetical.

evidence.detail: Restoration refuses a project already containing records or history.
The initial survey is an ordinary empty object.
survey[story.id] accepts inherited properties without an own-property check.

impact.reason: The real scene generator throws TypeError for inherited IDs when no own survey entry exists. This prevents that scene update; persistent full-desktop unavailability was not demonstrated.

evidence.detail: A non-undefined inherited value reaches survey.files.length and throws.
view.show is reached only after forestScene succeeds.
Reader error handling can retain a previously displayed scene.

counterevidence: Normal planning does not expose caller-selected story IDs.
Restoration refuses nonempty projects, limiting the affected target.
The source identifies snapshots as backups; inspected restoration tests use owner-generated snapshots.
An own survey entry masks the inherited property; that control passed.
No prototype mutation or code execution was observed.
test_evidence: challenge-map.mts passed, exit 0: real forestScene threw for __proto__, constructor and toString with an ordinary empty survey.
An ordinary ID, a null-prototype survey and explicit own survey entries all rendered successfully.
The real story-fields schema rejected an explicit id field in challenge-publication.mts.
test_limitations: Restoration, database persistence and full desktop behavior were not executed.
The restoration-to-tree chain is static evidence.
External snapshot acceptance and supplier trust remain unknown.
verdicts.remediation: Use own-property checks or Map-based survey lookups and safe empty dictionaries. Validate restored identifiers or ensure all readers safely handle arbitrary string IDs.
verdicts.regression_test_recommendation: Retain ordinary-ID, inherited-ID and own-entry controls. Require absent surveys to remain absent for __proto__, constructor and toString. Separately test restoration serialization through a mocked storage boundary without a live database.

limitations: Review scope was the supplied source snapshot and this job’s newly generated evidence; candidate evidence and other reviewers’ outputs were not used.

Both probes used the mandated submitter and isolated real imports. Their result.json files preserve the pinned commit, exact execution command, script hash and exit status; stdout.txt and stderr.txt preserve output.
No large-input execution, full suites, builds, browser execution, database operations, network research or live services were used.
Deployment CSP, external recording/backup acceptance, recipient filesystem authorization and restricted project-writer roles could not be established from the reviewed source.
